title: Visit-notes editor saves a stale whole VisitRecording and can erase a transcript that arrived while the sheet was open
trigger: On RecordingDetailView, tap 'Transcribe saved audio' (async, isProviderBusy does not disable 'Edit visit notes'), then open 'Edit visit notes' while transcription runs. Transcription completes and AppStore.transcribeRecording saves segments/transcriptionModel/status='transcribed' (AppStore+Transcription.swift:36-39). Tap Save in the notes sheet.
expected: Only VisitRecording.summary (the separate notes field) changes; the transcript segments, transcriptionModel and status saved a moment earlier remain (header contract: 'does not alter transcript words or audio').
actual: RecordingNotesEditor holds '@State var recording' initialised once from the sheet's initial value (line 15) and Save calls store.save(recording) (line 26); AppStore.save(_ recording:) replaces the whole element by id (AppStore+Recordings.swift:11-19). The stale draft (segments=[], transcriptionModel=nil, status='saved') overwrites the freshly saved transcript. The 'Transcribe saved audio' button is disabled only while segments are non-empty (RecordingDetailView.swift:77-79), so the transcript can be regenerated only by paying for another provider call; if a memory existed it keeps the transcript text until the next 'Update memory', which then rebuilds it from notes only.
impact: Loss of a paid Whisper transcript on a realistic overlap (user takes notes while waiting for transcription). Same last-writer-wins shape would also drop a segments change arriving from a sync pull while the sheet is open.
evidence: Source: RecordingNotesEditor.swift:15,26 (sed -n verified); AppStore+Recordings.swift:11-19 whole-object replace; RecordingDetailView.swift:74-80 (transcribe Task) and :127-128 ('Edit visit notes' not disabled during isProviderBusy) and :140-142 (sheet content re-evaluated but @State initial value is not reapplied); AppStore+Transcription.swift:18-20 shows the transcription path itself re-reads 'latest' before saving, i.e. the store already models this overlap as possible. Refutation attempt: checked whether SwiftUI recreates the editor state when the parent's 'recording' changes; State(initialValue:) applies only on first identity creation, so the draft stays stale. Contrast: TranscriptTextEditor + saveMemory guard Set(ids) == Set(keys) and reject a changed transcript (AppStore+Recordings.swift:49-55); the notes path has no equivalent guard.
smallestFix: Save notes through a field-targeted mutation, e.g. AppStore.updateRecordingNotes(id:summary:) that mutates only data.recordings[i].summary inside mutate; RecordingNotesEditor keeps only the recording ID plus a String draft. Optionally also disable 'Edit visit notes' while isProviderBusy.
regressionCheck: Isolated macOS AppStore harness (pattern in docs/task-specs/transcript-correction.md): create recording R with no segments; capture a notes draft; save R with two segments and transcriptionModel; apply the notes save with the stale draft; assert R.segments.count == 2, transcriptionModel unchanged, summary == draft notes.

title: A failed finish() leaves the recorder in a dead-end paused state whose only guidance is contradictory
trigger: finish() throws after stopping the recorder: verification fails because the file is empty/shorter than 0.1 s (Start then Finish within ~100 ms, or an input that produced no encoded frames), or AVAudioPlayer(contentsOf:) rejects a file left unfinalised after mediaServicesWereReset/encode error (both paths already set reachedEnd = true and tell the user to 'Save what was captured').
expected: Either the capture stays resumable so the user can 'record a little longer' as the emptyRecording message advises, or the recorder moves to an explicit terminal state with a single accurate instruction (discard and start again).
actual: finish() stops the AVAudioRecorder, sets isPaused = true and reachedEnd = true and releases the session before verification (lines 205-211); on failure it only sets errorMessage and rethrows (224-227), leaving isRecording == true and recorder != nil. The view then shows 'Paused' with Resume/Finish buttons. resume() hits 'guard !reachedEnd' and reports 'The one-hour recording limit was reached. Save this recording before starting another.' (lines 178-182) even though no time limit was reached; Finish repeats the same failure; start() throws .busy (line 111). The only exit is Close -> 'Discard recording'.
impact: Contradictory, incorrect user guidance on the failure path of the main recording flow (message says record longer; resume says one-hour limit reached; discard is the only way out). No data loss beyond the already-unusable draft.
evidence: Source lines verified with sed -n: AudioServices.swift:26 (emptyRecording text), :176-182 (resume guard and one-hour text), :202-228 (finish state changes before verification, catch does not reset state), :111 (start busy guard). RecordingSessionView.swift:42-46 renders Resume/Finish while isRecording. Refutation attempt: looked for any path that clears reachedEnd or recorder after a failed finish; only cancel()/cleanUpDraft() do (lines 232-253), which delete the draft.
smallestFix: In finish()'s catch, transition to an explicit terminal state (e.g. a 'finishFailed' flag) and have resume() report 'This recording could not be finalised; discard it and start a new recording'; change the emptyRecording text to match (do not promise 'record a little longer'). Alternatively perform verification before setting reachedEnd and only mark terminal when the stop actually happened.
regressionCheck: Unit-style harness on AudioRecorder with an injected empty draft: after finish() throws, assert resume() publishes the finalisation message (not the one-hour text) and that cancel() returns to the ready state; UI check that the session screen offers a discard/restart action.

title: Camera scan path allows 30 pages but assembles full-resolution pages into a PDF on the main actor and then applies the 16 MiB byte cap with a message that does not fit the camera path
trigger: On a physical iPhone, scan several pages with 'Scan a document' (VNDocumentCameraViewController) and tap Save in the scanner.
expected: A multi-page camera scan within the advertised page limit imports successfully, or is rejected with a message that tells the user what to do on this path (fewer pages); memory use is bounded by downsampling before PDF assembly.
actual: DocumentScanner accepts up to DocumentImportService.maximumPages (30) and materialises every page image at once (line 56-60). AddRecordView draws each full-resolution UIImage into a UIGraphicsPDFRenderer inside a MainActor Task (AddRecordView.swift:143-165), writes the PDF to tmp and calls ingest(url:), which rejects anything over 16 MiB with 'This file exceeds the 16 MB import limit. Export a smaller copy and try again.' (DocumentImportService.swift:47-48,120,131). Nothing downsamples scan pages (OCR downsampling at 2600 px happens only after the bytes are accepted). Camera page images are several megapixels each; Core Graphics embeds non-JPEG-backed bitmaps with Flate, so a handful of pages can exceed the cap while the page limit still says 30.
impact: Multi-page camera scans on hardware are likely rejected well below the advertised page limit with unactionable guidance, after a main-thread PDF assembly whose peak memory scales with page count x full-resolution bitmap size (concrete resource argument: N pages x W x H x 4 bytes held simultaneously plus the Flate-encoded PDF Data). Exact page count at which rejection occurs is unmeasured (hardware check unavailable to this audit).
evidence: Source: DocumentScanner.swift:52-60 (page limit and eager image materialisation), AddRecordView.swift:143-165 (full-size draw, main-actor Task), DocumentImportService.swift:70,117-135 (16 MiB stream bound), :47-48 (message). Refutation attempt: searched for any downsampling or JPEG re-encode between the scanner callback and ingest; none exists. The pixel size and backing (JPEG vs bitmap) of VNDocumentCameraScan.imageOfPage output is not verifiable from source; see evidence request EV-05-02 for a bounded macOS measurement of the CG PDF encoder behaviour.
smallestFix: Before PDF assembly, resize each scan page to at most DocumentImportService.maximumOCREdge (2600 px) and JPEG-encode it (UIImage.jpegData ~0.7), draw the JPEG-backed image into the PDF off the main actor (or ingest the JPEG pages directly), and give the scan path its own error text ('Scan fewer pages'). Align the scanner page limit with what the byte cap can hold.
regressionCheck: Harness: build a PDF from 10 synthetic 3024x4032 page images through the same code path and assert the resulting Data.count < 16 MiB; UI check on hardware that a 10-page scan imports and shows 10 pageTexts slots.

title: A 20-character embedded-text threshold skips OCR for scanned pages that carry only a short text banner, with no page warning
trigger: Import a scanned PDF whose pages are images plus a small embedded text line of >= 20 characters (fax header 'Received 2026-09-12 14:03 Page 1/4', scanner date stamp, or a 'CONFIDENTIAL' footer).
expected: Pages whose embedded text is negligible relative to the page are OCR'd (within the 10-page OCR budget) or at least flagged so the reviewer knows recognition was skipped.
actual: extractPDF uses the embedded text whenever it is >= 20 characters and never rasterises the page (line 256-257), so the page's image content is silently absent from text/pageTexts and no OCR warning is attached (the ocrReviewWarning is added only when OCR runs, line 265). The review screen shows only the banner text; search and brief selection cannot see the page content.
impact: Extracted text for a common class of medical documents (faxed/scanned records with text stamps) is the stamp only; nothing tells the user that OCR was skipped for those pages. Original bytes are preserved and the text is user-reviewable, so this is a robustness/quality issue rather than data loss. docs/task-specs/device-services.md:101 documents the heuristic as a known limitation but the app does not surface it.
evidence: Source: DocumentImportService.swift:256-278 (sed -n verified). Refutation attempt: checked whether any later step compares embedded-text density to page area or adds a warning; none (limitedText and the empty-text warnings only trigger on empty results).
smallestFix: Treat embedded text as sufficient only when it is substantial for the page (e.g. >= ~200 characters, or characters per point^2 above a small density), otherwise OCR within the existing budget and keep the longer result (line 278 already does this); when OCR is skipped for a short-text page, append a per-page warning ('Page N has little embedded text and was not scanned with OCR').
regressionCheck: Harness PDF: page with a full-size text image plus a 30-character embedded header; assert pageTexts[0] contains the image text and the OCR review warning is present.

title: Playback of a synced browser recording in an unsupported container (WebM/Ogg) reports 'missing or damaged' instead of unsupported format
trigger: A recording created in the browser client (audioFilename ending .webm or .ogg; apps/web/src/core/store.ts:59-60 maps these extensions) is pulled to the iPhone via explicit sync (AppStore+Sync.swift:76-78 pulls recordings' audio); tap Play on RecordingDetailView.
expected: The message states that this recording format cannot be played on this device and that the original file is preserved/shareable (docs/architecture.md:189 already says playback 'depends on the receiving device').
actual: play(url:) wraps any AVAudioPlayer(contentsOf:) failure or invalid duration in DeviceAudioError.invalidAudio, whose text is 'This audio file could not be played. It may be missing or damaged.' (lines 27, 400-403, 417-420). The file exists and is intact; AVFoundation does not decode WebM/Ogg containers.
impact: Misleading claim of a damaged medical recording on the cross-client path; user may believe the original is lost. Codec/hardware behaviour itself is unverified in this audit (no device/simulator available), but the message path is source-proven for any init failure.
evidence: Source: AudioServices.swift:27,393-421 (sed -n verified); ServerClient.swift:67-75 shows the native client knowingly labels webm/ogg for transport; RecordingDetailView.swift:29-58 shows the play control for any audioFilename. Refutation attempt: looked for an extension/UTType check before AVAudioPlayer init; none.
smallestFix: Before constructing AVAudioPlayer, check the URL's extension against the AVFoundation-playable set (m4a/mp4/wav/mp3/caf) and throw a distinct DeviceAudioError.unsupportedFormat with text such as 'This recording was made in the browser in a format iPhone cannot play. The original is kept; share it to play elsewhere.'
regressionCheck: Harness: play(url:) on a synthetic .webm file must publish the unsupported-format message, not 'missing or damaged'; play on a valid .caf tone still succeeds (existing harness check).

title: Exported visit-brief PDF hard-codes the legacy teal (#0A5B6C) instead of the heart-red palette
trigger: Export any visit brief ('Share visit brief').
expected: Exported headings/header use the final heart-red palette (accent #B84250 / deep red #8C2F3B per RevaTheme in Features/Shared/Theme.swift:13-22) or a deliberate print-neutral colour; token naming reflects the current design.
actual: ReportPDFRenderer draws the title, section headings, 'Sources' heading and running header in a private static 'teal' UIColor(10/255, 91/255, 108/255) (lines 126,133,141,181,208-210), a colour from the superseded teal design (docs/verification/README.md:1 states older teal captures are not the current design).
impact: Visual identity mismatch between app and its exported artifact; misleading token name. No functional effect on citations, pagination or staleness.
evidence: Source: ReportPDFRenderer.swift:208-210 (sed -n verified) and call sites at 126/133/141/181; Theme.swift:13-22 for the current tokens.
smallestFix: Replace the private 'teal' with a UIColor built from the RevaTheme deep-red/heart-red hex values (or route through a shared UIKit colour helper) and rename the property.
regressionCheck: Render a PDF in the harness and sample the header pixel colour (existing harness already samples colour pixels per docs/task-specs/device-services.md:85).

title: loadSample(visitID:) ignores its visitID parameter, so the API implies per-visit sample attachment that never happens
trigger: Tap 'Explore sample transcript' on any visit other than the fixture visit demo-visit-primary-20260908 (VisitDetailView.swift:122-129 passes the current visit id).
expected: The function signature reflects the behaviour: the sample is always attached to its own fixture visit (which is the correct, documented separation from real audio).
actual: The parameter is unused; the sample is decoded from sample-transcript.json, always bound to sample.visitID, and the user is navigated to a recording that is not listed under the visit they were viewing (VisitDetailView filters recordings by visitID at line 130).
impact: Cleanliness/API honesty only (B05-type). Behaviour is safe: new audio never receives the sample and the sample never gets an audioFilename (lines 34-36).
smallestFix: Drop the parameter (loadSample()) or rename to make the fixture binding explicit; optionally show a notice that the sample lives on its fixture visit when opened from another visit.
regressionCheck: Compile; existing behaviour (existing sample id returned, no audioFilename) unchanged.

title: After a successful finish(), a failed metadata save orphans the finalised audio with no retry path
trigger: recorder.finish() succeeds (ownership of the .m4a transfers to the caller, AudioServices.swift:217-223) and store.save(recording) then throws (repository write failure, or snapshot validation such as the visit no longer existing).
expected: The finalised audio URL is retained by the screen and a 'Retry save' action is offered, or the file is at least referenced so it can be recovered.
actual: store.perform reports the error; savedID stays nil and recorder.isRecording is false, so the view falls back to the consent toggle and 'Start recording' (lines 47-63). The finished file remains in the attachments directory unreferenced; recorder.audioURL still holds it (AudioServices.swift:222) but the view never uses it.
impact: Rare-path robustness: a completed capture becomes unreachable from the app after a save failure. Files are not deleted (consistent with the retained-originals policy).
smallestFix: Keep the finished URL in view state when save fails and render a 'Retry saving recording' button that re-runs only store.save(recording) with the same VisitRecording value.
regressionCheck: Harness with a failing repository double: finish then save failure, then retry succeeds and the VisitRecording references the same audioFilename.

title: PDF export runs Core Text pagination and PDF writing synchronously on the main actor up to 200,000 characters / 100 pages; cost unmeasured
trigger: Export a brief near the renderer's ceiling (many long sources; the AI overview plus up to 100 candidate records can approach 200k characters).
expected: Either a measured bound showing the main-thread stall is negligible at the ceiling, or rendering moved off the main actor with a progress state.
actual: ReportPDFRenderer is @MainActor and ReportView.exportReport calls it inside store.perform synchronously (ReportView.swift:99-126). Each page is laid out twice (measure loop lines 63-81, draw loop 98-111). Layout is O(characters); the ceiling is bounded (200k chars, 100 pages) so this is finite, but no measurement exists in the evidence directory.
impact: Potential UI freeze of unknown length during export at large inputs. Not a defect until measured; recorded as an efficiency evidence gap per M01.
evidence: Source: ReportPDFRenderer.swift:34-35,38-39,63-81,96-112 (sed -n verified). No evidence/commands.jsonl entries exist at review time. See evidence request EV-05-01 (bounded macOS Core Text proxy measurement).
smallestFix: If EV-05-01 shows >= ~0.3 s at the ceiling: make render(...) nonisolated/async (Core Text and UIGraphicsPDFRenderer are usable off the main thread for offscreen work) and show the existing ProgressView pattern while exporting.
regressionCheck: Harness timing of render() with a 200k-character body stays under an agreed budget, or the export runs off the main actor with the UI responsive.

title: Re-saving an unchanged memory discards a connected-AI summary of the memory record and bumps its version, staling briefs for no source change
trigger: Save a visit memory, open the memory record and use 'Summarize with Gemini' (RecordDetailView.swift:66-70 offers it for any record with text), then tap 'Update memory in Records' again without changing the transcript or notes.
expected: An idempotent re-save leaves an unchanged memory alone (text, summary, summaryModel, version) so dependent briefs do not go stale.
actual: saveMemory unconditionally sets record.summary = localExcerpt(sourceText) and record.summaryModel = nil (lines 96-97); because previous.summary != record.summary the version increments (lines 116-119), and ReportEngine.signature includes summary and version, so every saved brief becomes stale although no source content changed.
impact: Loss of a paid summary and spurious staleness on an idempotent action; labels remain honest ('Local excerpt'). Minor.
evidence: Source: AppStore+Recordings.swift:94-97,116-119 (sed -n verified); ReportEngine.swift:41-42 (signature inputs). Refutation attempt: checked whether the text-unchanged case short-circuits; it does not.
smallestFix: Only reset summary/summaryModel when record.text actually changes (compare previous.text before assigning); keep the version rule as is.
regressionCheck: Harness: save memory, set summaryModel on the record, call saveMemory again with no change; assert summaryModel and version unchanged.
